Now I have all the information needed to produce the correctness review. I've read all the implementation files, tests, ADOPT-001 §12.8, DECISIONS.md D-044, and STATUS.md, and compared them against the plan-doc invariants and DISPATCH-NOTE specification.

{"round":"R5","lens":"correctness","slice":"WP-SCP-024-024B","work_package":"WP-SCP-024","verdict":"BLOCKED","new_crit_count":0,"new_maj_count":3,"new_min_count":2,"new_nit_count":1,"summary":"No CRIT found. Three MAJ identified. First: an unresolved gap from the initial R1 round — the `onboarded-operator-bump` first guard (`branch_log_modified == 0 → die`) is never exercised in the failing direction; cases 4c–4f all write to the log before committing, so every STATUS.md-failing case also passes the log-modified guard; the path where an operator declares operator-bump but omits the enable-required-check.sh invocation is untested. Second: `make_output_dir()` creates `out.XXXXXX` dirs directly under `REPO_ROOT`, outside the `TMPDIR` the EXIT trap cleans up; git status confirms two leaked dirs (`out.KUChNE/`, `out.xHr6c6/`) with no `.gitignore` pattern to suppress them, so any test failure mid-run leaves permanent artifacts. Third: the `--scp-sha` warn-but-continue path (valid SHA that is not main HEAD) has no test coverage — all happy-path invocations use `rev-parse HEAD`, guaranteeing SHA == main HEAD. Two MIN: `die \"could not parse log entry target\"` in `check-invocation-log-entry.sh` is dead code under `set -euo pipefail`; and the `--restore` guard omits `--expected-wrapper-sha` from its forward-mode exclusion check, silently ignoring the flag in restore mode. One nit on an ambiguous test error message.","findings":[{"id":"R5-COR-MAJ-001","severity":"MAJ","claim":"test_check_invocation_log_entry.sh has no test case for `cascade-status: onboarded-operator-bump` with an UNMODIFIED branch-protection log, leaving the first guard in the operator-bump check path (branch_log_modified == 0 → die) permanently untested in its failure direction.","evidence":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh line 193: `[ \"$branch_log_modified\" -eq 1 ] || die \"ERROR: branch-protection-log.md was not modified for cascade-status=onboarded-operator-bump\"`. Cases 4a, 4c, 4d, 4e, 4f, 4g, 4h all write to branch-protection-log.md before `commit_case`, so `branch_log_modified=1` in every operator-bump scenario. The analogous negative for `onboarded` exists (case2, line 220). The analogous negative for `blocked-on-adopter-conflict` exists (case10, line 434). This specific guard was flagged in the R1 round (R1-COR-MAJ-002) but remains unaddressed.","impact":"A refactor that accidentally removes or inverts the log-modified guard for operator-bump passes all tests. More critically, an operator could declare `cascade-status: onboarded-operator-bump` with a passing STATUS.md TF row but without running enable-required-check.sh, and CI would pass — violating plan-doc invariant 2 ('Required-check enablement is operator-run + invocation-logged + CI-enforced') for the higher-risk operator-driven path.","mitigation":"Add a case: init_case_repo, write DISPATCH-NOTE with `cascade-status: onboarded-operator-bump` and valid Target line, write STATUS.md with a regex-passing TF row, do NOT modify branch-protection-log.md (leave it empty as init_case_repo commits it), then `commit_case` and `run_case ... 1 '' 'ERROR: branch-protection-log.md was not modified for cascade-status=onboarded-operator-bump'`."},{"id":"R5-COR-MAJ-002","severity":"MAJ","claim":"`make_output_dir()` in test_scaffold_downstream.sh creates `out.XXXXXX` directories directly under `REPO_ROOT`; the EXIT trap only removes `$TMPDIR`, so leaked artifacts accumulate on test failure and have no .gitignore coverage.","evidence":"test_scaffold_downstream.sh line 86-88: `make_output_dir() { mktemp -d \"${REPO_ROOT}/out.XXXXXX\"; }`. EXIT trap at line 10-13: `cleanup() { rm -rf \"$TMPDIR\"; }`. `.gitignore` has no `out.*` or `out/` pattern (confirmed by reading root .gitignore: only .pytest_cache, __pycache__, .venv, *.pyc, .DS_Store, .scp/, *.egg-info, ~$*). Git status at conversation start confirms two leaked dirs from prior runs: `?? ../../../../out.KUChNE/` and `?? ../../../../out.xHr6c6/` (relative to docs/reviews/WP-SCP-024/024B, these are REPO_ROOT/out.*).","impact":"Every failed or interrupted test run leaves permanent untracked directories under REPO_ROOT, polluting `git status` indefinitely and confusing future PR reviewers who see unexpected `??` entries. Multiple test runs accumulate more leaked dirs. Because the dirs contain wrapper YAML and manifest JSON derived from real SHAs, they may also contain sensitive test artifacts.","mitigation":"Change `make_output_dir` to create under `$TMPDIR` (already cleaned by the trap): `mktemp -d \"${TMPDIR}/out.XXXXXX\"`. Alternatively keep REPO_ROOT creation but track all outdirs explicitly: `OUTDIRS=(); make_output_dir() { local d; d=\"$(mktemp -d \"${REPO_ROOT}/out.XXXXXX\")\"; OUTDIRS+=(\"$d\"); printf '%s' \"$d\"; }` and extend cleanup to `rm -rf \"$TMPDIR\" \"${OUTDIRS[@]:-}\"`. Also add `out.*/` to `.gitignore` as a belt-and-suspenders guard."},{"id":"R5-COR-MAJ-003","severity":"MAJ","claim":"`test_scaffold_downstream.sh` has no test for the explicit plan-doc behavior 'warns when SHA is not main HEAD but continues': all happy-path invocations use `rev-parse HEAD`, guaranteeing SHA == main HEAD and never triggering the non-HEAD warn path.","evidence":"test_scaffold_downstream.sh line 7: `SCP_SHA=\"$(git -C \"${REPO_ROOT}\" rev-parse HEAD)\"`. scaffold-downstream.sh lines 142-147: `MAIN_HEAD_SHA=\"$(git -C \"$SCP_REPO_ROOT\" rev-parse main 2>/dev/null || true)\"; ... elif [ \"$SCP_SHA\" != \"$MAIN_HEAD_SHA\" ]; then warn \"--scp-sha $SCP_SHA is not current SCP main HEAD...\"; fi`. Because all test invocations use the current HEAD SHA, `SCP_SHA == MAIN_HEAD_SHA` always, so the warn block at line 145-147 is never executed during tests. Plan-doc §5.3 + DISPATCH-NOTE scope table both explicitly specify this warn behavior.","impact":"A regression that accidentally converts the warn into a hard exit (exit 1 instead of continue) would break all cascade slice invocations that pin to any SHA other than the live main HEAD — including all historical cascade re-invocations. The regression would be silent in CI tests, discovered only when an operator runs the script with a non-HEAD SHA in production.","mitigation":"Add a test case: obtain a valid non-HEAD SHA via `git -C \"${REPO_ROOT}\" rev-parse HEAD^` (parent of HEAD, guaranteed to exist in any non-empty repo), invoke scaffold-downstream.sh with that SHA, assert exit 0, assert stderr contains 'is not current SCP main HEAD', and assert all 4 output files are present."},{"id":"R5-COR-MIN-001","severity":"MIN","claim":"`die \"ERROR: could not parse the log entry target from the branch-protection diff\"` at check-invocation-log-entry.sh line 188 is unreachable dead code under `set -euo pipefail`: a non-zero exit from `parse_entry_repo` causes `set -e` to terminate the script at the assignment line before the die guard is evaluated.","evidence":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh line 182-183: `entry_repo=\"$(printf '%s' \"$branch_log_patch\" | parse_entry_repo)\"` — with `set -euo pipefail`, if `parse_entry_repo` exits 1, the assignment command itself returns non-zero and `set -e` fires immediately. Line 188: `[ -n \"$entry_repo\" ] || die \"ERROR: could not parse the log entry target from the branch-protection diff\"` is never reached. `parse_entry_repo` emits its own stderr message (`ERROR: expected exactly one log entry target match, found N: ...`) before exiting 1. test case17 (line 639) correctly checks for the parse_entry_repo error string, confirming the die message is never the visible output.","impact":"Not a silent failure — errors propagate correctly via parse_entry_repo's stderr + set -e. However, the die message is documented as the expected error signal for this path but is never shown; any tooling or operator runbook that expects that specific string will not match. The die guard also provides no value as a fallback safety net.","mitigation":"Convert to explicit error capture: `entry_repo=\"$(printf '%s' \"$branch_log_patch\" | parse_entry_repo)\" || die \"ERROR: could not parse the log entry target from the branch-protection diff\"`. The `||` suppresses `set -e` on the command substitution failure, allowing the die message to execute with the correct exit 1."},{"id":"R5-COR-MIN-002","severity":"MIN","claim":"`--restore` mode standalone guard in `enable-required-check.sh` line 210 does not exclude `--expected-wrapper-sha`, allowing the forward-mode-only SHA-pin verification flag to be silently combined with `--restore` and ignored.","evidence":"enable-required-check.sh line 210-214: the restore-mode guard checks `REPO`, `BRANCH`, `PLAN_ONLY`, `ACK_ADMIN_BYPASS`, `ACK_NO_PRIOR_GREEN_CI`, and `ENFORCE_ADMINS != \"true\"` — but NOT `EXPECTED_WRAPPER_SHA`. Arg parser at line 195 sets `EXPECTED_WRAPPER_SHA=\"$2\"` for `--expected-wrapper-sha`. The wrapper-pin check is inside `if [ -z \"$RESTORE_STATE\" ]` (line 253), so it never executes in restore mode. Combined invocation `--restore X --expected-wrapper-sha SHA` silently proceeds as restore-only, giving the operator a false sense that the SHA pin was verified before re-arming.","impact":"An operator following ADOPT-001 §12.8 Gate 3 who passes `--expected-wrapper-sha` along with `--restore` by mistake (e.g., copy-pasting from a forward-mode invocation) receives no error and believes the SHA check ran. The Gate 3 precondition verification step is silently skipped. Low probability in practice since the flags serve opposite phases of the break-glass procedure.","mitigation":"Add `|| [ -n \"$EXPECTED_WRAPPER_SHA\" ]` to the restore-mode forward-flag exclusion guard at line 210, so combined invocations produce: `error: --restore is a standalone mode and cannot be combined with forward-mode flags`."},{"id":"R5-COR-nit-001","severity":"nit","claim":"`validate_manifest` in test_scaffold_downstream.sh line 71 raises `SystemExit(\"manifest should list 3 emitted files\")` without clarifying that the manifest intentionally excludes itself (4 files emitted, 3 listed in manifest).","evidence":"test_scaffold_downstream.sh line 70-72: `if len(payload[\"files\"]) != 3: raise SystemExit(\"manifest should list 3 emitted files\")`. The script emits 4 files (wrapper, CODEOWNERS-snippet, CASCADE-PR-BODY, MANIFEST.json) but MANIFEST.json lists only 3 (excluding itself — a self-referential SHA would be circular). The error message `\"manifest should list 3 emitted files\"` reads as if only 3 files exist, not as if 3-of-4 are listed because the manifest cannot hash itself.","impact":"A reader of a failing validate_manifest error would incorrectly conclude the scaffolder should emit only 3 files, potentially leading them to add a redundant 4th file or remove the self-hash exclusion. Low operational risk.","mitigation":"Change to: `raise SystemExit(\"manifest.files should list 3 of 4 emitted files (MANIFEST.json does not hash itself)\")`."}]}
